title.narrative: UPPSALA UNIV 2022 - 2025: Medborgarperspektiv på samhällsutmaningar i Mali
UPPSALA UNIV 2022 - 2026: Citizens perspectives on societal challenges in Mali

description.narrative:
Programmet Citizens' Perspectives on Social Challenges syftar till att främja medborgarnas perspektiv genom implementering av engagerad forskning, organisering av medborgardebatter och kapacitetsbyggande aktiviteter. Inom ramen för ett partnerskap mellan malisk-svenska forskarlag kommer programmet att fokusera på nyckelfrågor identifierade i den svenska samarbetsstrategin för Mali 2021-2025. Särskild uppmärksamhet kommer att ägnas åt främjandet av kvinnliga ledare som forskare, lärare och opinionsbildare.
Programmet var initialt utformat för fem år (2021-2025) med en total budget på 19 MSEK. Programmet inkluderar även finansiering av gemensamma projekt i form av "såddpengar" för att stödja implementeringen av malisk-svenska forskarlag.
Programmet kommer att vara uppdelat i två delar:
1) Den första komponenten syftar till att genomföra strategiska studier och medborgardebatter, inklusive dokumentation och analys av medborgarperspektiv på de utmaningar som det maliska samhället står inför. Resultaten av de strategiska studierna kommer sedan att presenteras för allmänheten och publiceras i form av böcker tillgängliga för icke-specialister, "briefs" eller poddsändningar/tv-sändningar på olika maliska språk. Tillvägagångssättet är iterativt i den meningen att medborgardebatterna också kommer att bidra till att identifiera teman och inriktningar för forskningen och studierna.
2) Den andra komponenten syftar till att nätverka maliska och svenska utbildningsforskningsinstitutioner för att utveckla partnerskap mellan forskarlag från båda länderna. Dessa partnerskap kan genomföra gemensamma projekt på forskningsteman som är prioriterade för den svenska samarbetsstrategin i Mali. Inom denna komponent kommer programmet också att anordna utbildningsworkshops på plats i Mali om forskningsmetodik, projektkonceptualisering, dataanalys och vetenskapligt skrivande.
Programmet kommer att koordineras av Forum för Afrikastudier vid Uppsala universitet (Sverige) i samarbete med Institut des Sciences Humaines(ISH) (Mali) baserat på det samarbete som redan pågår inom Laboratoire d'Anthropologie Comparative, Engagée et Transnationale (LACET) ). Kom ihåg att programmet bygger på befintliga partnerskap sedan 2008 mellan Uppsala universitet och maliska forskningsinstitutioner (Point Sud, ISFRA, ISH).

The Citizens' Perspectives on Social Challenges program aims to promote citizen's perspectives through the implementation of engaged research, the organization of citizen debates and capacity building activities. Within the framework of a partnership between Malian-Swedish research teams, the program will focus on key issues identified in the 2021- 2025 Swedish cooperation strategy for Mali. Special attention will be given to the promotion of women leaders as researchers, teachers and opinion leaders.
Designed initially for five years (2021-2025) with a total budget of 19 MSEK, the program includes also the funding for joint projects in the form of "seed money" to support the implementation of Malian-Swedish research teams.
The program will be organized in two components:
1) The first component aims to implement strategic studies and citizen debates, including the documentation and analysis of citizen perspectives on the challenges facing Malian society. The results of the strategic studies will be then presented to the general public and published in the form of books accessible to non-specialists, "briefs" or podcasts/television broadcasts in different Malian languages. The approach is iterative in the sense that the citizens' debates will also help identify the themes and orientations of the research and studies.
2) The second component aims to network Malian and Swedish educational research institutions in order to develop partnerships between research teams from both countries. These partnerships can implement joint projects on research themes that are priorities for the Swedish cooperation strategy in Mali. Within this component, the program will also organize on-site training workshops in Mali on research methodology, project conceptualization, data analysis and scientific writing.
The program will be coordinated by the Forum for Africa Studies at Uppsala University (Sweden) in partnership with the Institut des Sciences Humaines(ISH) (Mali) based on the collaboration already underway within the Laboratoire d'Anthropologie Comparative, Engagée et Transnationale (LACET). Remember that the program is built on existing partnerships since 2008 between Uppsala University and Malian research institutions (Point Sud, ISFRA, ISH).

This project is quite unique in different ways. It is a research collaboration funded through the bilateral development cooperation strategy that doesn't include research. The Embassy decided to fund it because it is a research collaboration where the research itself as well as the findings are used for dialogue with different stakeholders. The main deliverables are not peer-reviewed scientific articles as is often the case with research projects. Instead the focus was to publish the results in formats that are accessible to the general public in the form of books written for non-specialists, briefs, podcasts/television programs etc. These were not seen as the final product but rather as discussion material for more dialogue, as was the data collection. The research conveys what "ordinary people" think about governance in Mali, what they have to say about women's participation at different levels of society etc. The project was also a way for Malian and Swedish researchers to meet around different research topics to form new collaborations.
Component 1 Engaged research (which includes public engagement and mutual benefit)
Publications
1. the book Résistance, alternance, souveraineté was published in 2024. It is important to remember that this book should not be seen as ONE output but the result of many important dialogue sessions that fed into it and that took place after it was published.
Hagberg, S., Coulibaly, B., Koné, Y. F., & Traoré, N. gna (Eds.). (2024). Résistance, alternance, souveraineté?: Une recherche engagée sur la crise et la transition au Mali. Retrieved from https://urn.kb.se/resolve?urn=urn:nbn:se:uu:diva-530823
The book has already received important reactions and positive feedback in Mali and internationally. Many Malian actors welcome the publication, particularly because it consitutes an attempt to describe, and analyze the last years' political change and events from below.
2. the book Comment briser le plafond de verre? (How to break the glass ceiling) was published in October 2025 (not reflected in the final report as it was published after the report was finalised):
Hagberg, S., Y.F. Koné, B. Koné, A. Sylla, F. Camara, B. Coulibaly, A. Diabaté, N. Traoré, L. Bello, M. Coulibaly, F. Diabaté, F. Fofana et M. Sidibé. 2025. Comment casser le plafond de verre ?: Une recherche engagée sur la participation politique des femmes maliennes. Uppsala Papers in Africa Studies 10. Uppsala: Uppsala University.
This is the first strategic study about women in politics in Mali. This study documents and analyzes the opportunities and constraints for women leaders to enter and engage in politics. The main research question is how, in what contexts, and under what conditions, Malian women politicians manage to break through the glass ceiling. To address this question, the authors seek to go beyond an analysis of the gaps between official discourses and daily practices in order to focus on practical norms, that is, actions and statements deemed legitimate and acceptable in society. For a long time and despite decades of information and awareness campaigns, political measures and legal actions, the political participation of women as elected representatives in parliament and municipal councils and as leaders in civil society has been very low in Mali. While the study focuses on how Malian women have been excluded from formal decision making spheres it also reveals a significant change. The adoption of Law 52 of 18 December 2015 established new standards for promoting gender equality when it comes to elected and nominative positions. Today, the number of women holding elected and nominative positions has increased considerably. The same is true for the National Transitional Council, the interim parliament since the fall of Ibrahim Boubacar Keïta's regime in August 2020. Therefore, the authors conclude, there is a silent or perhaps better low noise transformation going on in the country, that goes under the radar of most observers, and analysts, let alone by the Malian public more generally.
3. Another publication will be published based on a strategic study on public women and insecurity. This publication, which in other words will be published after the end of the project will surely be very interesting as the fieldwork was done in high insecurity areas.
4. The fourth publication will also be published after the end of the project and it will be based on a study called When the donors have left. It will analyze what happens in local areas when international donors and NGOs pull out, due to geopolitical, and/or security reasons. The study is about how local actors handle the situation when projects have ended at a moment when the country is going through very difficult times.
It should be noted that the third and fourth publications above were not finalised during the project due to the shortened activity period due to the Swedish government's decision to end its development cooperation but the authors together with Uppsala University are committed to finalising them anyway. In the case of the third publication only the proofreading remained when this completion memo was drafted and when it comes to the fourth the fieldwork was done and the writeup remained.
Presentations
In May 2023, Professor Sten Hagberg, project leader gave a lecture on Malian women politicians at Folke Bernadotte Academy.
At the African Studies Associations Meeting in San Francisco in December 2023, Hagberg co organized a round table entitled Understanding the Resurgence of Sahelian Coups: A Grounded and Long term Interdisciplinary Perspective with Prof. William Moseley (Macalester College) Dr. Asmao Diallo Doshisha University) Dr. Boubacar Haïdara (Bonn International Centre for Conflict Studies) and Dr. Lisa Mueller (Macalester College)
Between 23 and 25 May 2024 Hagberg presented results from the study of Malian Women s Political Participation at the Forum de Bamako.
In December 2024 Hagberg gave a key note address drawing on the work in Burkina Faso, and Mali at the conference Lenquête de terrain à lépreuve des crises: enjeux épistémologiques et éthiques et innovations méthodologiques in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.
Hagberg attended the German Association for Africa Studies Conference on Reconfigurations in Africa and in African Studies in Bayreuth, Germany in September-October 2024.
Postings and discussions in social media. Information also shared via The Mande Studies Associations Facebook and Website www.mandestudies.org and the LACETs website: www.lacet.org.
Component 2: Developing partnerships
The project aimed to develop partnerships between Malian and Swedish researchers. In April 2023 a research workshop took place where the objective was for Malian and Swedish researchers to present their work in order to identify common areas of interest for the development of possible collaborative projects that the intervention had limited seed money for. Project proposals were analysed at the end of 2023 and in December 2023 a decision was taken to support seven of these seed money projects (seven out of eleven proposals) with SEK 300 000 each. On the 21st of December 2023 the Swedish government decided to end its development cooperation with Mali by the end of 2024 which means all workplans had to be adjusted but with the same budget. One additional project (an 8th project), led by a Malian IT-scientist together with a Swedish professor started as a result of the above-mentioned workshop but without seed funding as it managed to secure funding early career funding from an institute in the UK.
The seed money projects and what they achieved (in some cases outputs will be produced after the end of this project) were:
1. Artisanal mining and sovereignty (Mine artisanale et soueraineté: problème global, perspectives citoyennes locales). Two workshops were held in November 2024, first a scientific writing workshop and thene a collaborative research workshop focusing on the project's theme. Articles were prepared for the scientific cournal Echogéo's special issue Mining crafts: Power and territorialization in the global south.
2. Agro-silvo-pastoral landscapes in Mali (Cadre d'exploitation et de gestion durable des ressources naturelles danns les paysages agro-silvo-pastoraux). The project should really be seen as a pilot and it focused on understanding landscape change, governance arrangements and links across scales in one single village (Sakoro). The project identified relevant shocks and changes that are relevant for local stakeholders. Through a participatory process aspirations and issues were identified and new strategies for sustainable resource exploitation and management with local stakeholders were formulated.
3. Young women's words of insecurity in Gao and Mopti (Les mots de l'ensécurité: Récits de jeunes femmes des cercles de Gao et Mopti). The project sought to break free from the dichotomy of women as victims of insecurity versus women as agens of security by examining women's own accounts of insecurity in their daily lives. The research team focused on the 15-30 age group. Several publications are planned.
4. Managing sites of displaced in Bamako (Problématique de gestion des sites de déplacés au Mali: cas de Bamako). The Malian-Swedish research team did a litterature study on scientific articles, study reports, press articles and online contents. They also did semi-structured interviews to collect life stories around the teme of citizenship in order to understand the journeys, difficulties and daily experiences on the sites. The team also observed the social reality of internally displaced people.
5. Citizen perception on the French military intervention and UN peace-keeping. The research team conducted semi-structured interviews to anlyse how citizens assess the performance of these missions and where such perceptions stem from. The project focused on Internally displaced people and state representatives.
6. Climate change and gender equality (Climate change and gender equality in Africa: linking evidence from the citizen's perspective and the macro-level to understand the mechanisms by which weather shocks affect gender equality in Mali). Due to diplomatic tensions between Sweden and Mali the team worked together in Dakar, Senegal. They showed that climate change significantly exacerbates gender inequality. Women in rural areas, especially those involved in agriculture and water collection, experience the gendered impacts of calimate shocks more acutely. The study found that economic strain, domestic violence, health burdens and barriers to education and economic opportunities were common themes that hindered women's abilityy to cope with climate change. Policy recommendations were presented.
7. Youth and women's democratic participation on social media (Internet access, youth and women's democratic participation on social media). Face-to-face and online interviews of young bloggers and vloggers were held. Results were presented at a hybrid seminar in Sweden and a workshop in Bamako. Findings include that there is a prevalent fear among interviewees regarding the political situation, leading to hesitation about participating in interviews. They expressed concerns over threats related to sensitive topics, exemplified by the recent arrests of political leaders and the suspension of political activities. Yet the male bloggers reported feeling freer and more active in speaking publicly compared to their female counterparts. Another finding concerns how the anti-cybercrime law imposes restrictions on respondents online freedom of expression. Furthermore, closing of legacy media outlets pushing journalists online. Moreover, diaspora bloggers are often in exile, facing threats of arrest from the cybercrime division of the judicial authority. Many bloggers have shifted their focus to human rights or lighter topics, as themes like corruption and poor governance are particularly sensitive. Additionally, blogging is often a secondary occupation for many, who also work as journalists, teachers, video editors, or in TV/radio reporting.
* Healthy Maman. A Malian IT-scientist together with a Swedish professor started the Healthy Maman project. This project created a cell phone app that reminds pregnant women to go and get a check-up of their pregnancies. The objective was to enhance antenatal care attendance among pregnant women in Mali, starting with one of the communes in Bamako. This project did not get seed funding from this initiative but was the result of a partnership that was established thanks to the above mentioned workshop and got early career funding from an institute in the UK.
The eight projects described briefly above brought together 16 Malian and 10 Swedish researchers who started to collaborate thanks to the seed money. A number of research assistants were also involved. These research teams will continue to collaborate in different ways and to varying degrees.
A conference called Towards a decolonization of knowledge in West Africa: history, actors and productions was organised 26-29 June 2024. It was jointly organized by Uppsala Universitys Forum for Africa Studies, the Institut des Sciences Humaines (ISH), the Laboratoire dAnthropologie Comparative, Engagée et Transnationale (LACET), and the Mande Studies Association (MANSA) with substantial support from the project. The conference venue was at the ISH, but the conference was also accessible online, in a full-scale hybrid mode. Out of 170 submissions, 130 papers were accepted and presented in 40 panels; 100 papers were presented in situ, and 30 online. The total number of participants was estimated at 700. The project funded the hybrid mode organization of the conference, including secured internet connection, high-quality cameras, and audio-visual system, the conference secretariat, as well as the participation of 25 African participants. The project staff was furthermore involved in the planning and implementation of the whole conference. This contribution, the Embassy of Sweden and Sida were very visible during this event. Many commented that Sweden was doing the right thing, by investing in engaged research on societal challenges. In addition, two international workshops were hosted the days before the conference: on Academic Writing on 20 June, and on the Trajectories of West African Female Researchers on 24 June (Appendix 4A and 4b). Both events drew some 70 participants respectively.
Between 16 and 17 December, the 2024 Sahel Symposium was organized in hybrid mode, and bilingual (French/English), at Uppsala University, and at the Institut des Sciences Humaines on Citizen Perspectives on Societal Challenges. The symposium brought together some 20 scholars working in, and on the Sahel with a particular focus on research carried out in Mali.
